PostSummary: Curated accounts romanticize an idealized past — homemaking, large families, and old-fashioned gender roles — as the faithful life, implying that modern Christians who live differently are compromised.
BiblicalResponse: There is nothing wrong with loving home, family, or tradition, and much that is beautiful in them. But godliness is not an aesthetic and not a decade: it is love for God and neighbor lived out in whatever time and place God put you. A filtered feed is not a standard for faithfulness, and no lifestyle brand gets to define what a faithful man or woman looks like — Scripture does.
